note: BirdNET names a class; GBIF is the app's spine; sometimes they disagree. Every entry here
is a decision a person made once, so it stays made and shows up in a diff rather than
being re-litigated on each run. Nothing is aliased automatically — an unaliased
disagreement is reported and refused, because a silently coarsened detection looks
exactly like a working bridge (build plan §3.5).
Two kinds live here, and the difference matters. A nomenclatural alias renames the same
organism and loses nothing. A lump maps a split BirdNET models onto the broader species
GBIF still recognises, which does lose information — the record will read as the parent

kind.Astur gentilis: nomenclature — the goshawk moved to Astur in recent checklists; GBIF still says Accipiter
kind.Tachyspiza badia: nomenclature — Accipiter split into Tachyspiza and others; GBIF has not adopted it
kind.Anarhynchus atrifrons: nomenclature — sand plovers moved to Anarhynchus; GBIF accepts Charadrius atrifrons
kind.Botaurus minutus: nomenclature — little bittern moved from Ixobrychus to Botaurus; GBIF still says Ixobrychus
kind.Thinornis dubius: nomenclature — little ringed plover moved to Thinornis; GBIF still says Charadrius
kind.Gyps rueppelli: spelling — GBIF holds the name as rueppellii, so the match came back FUZZY
kind.Phylloscopus sibilatrix: spelling — GBIF itself holds the wood warbler as sibillatrix, with two l's
kind.Chloris chloris: nomenclature — GBIF files the greenfinch under Carduelis chloris and resolves it to the accepted key
kind.Cecropis rufula: LUMP — BirdNET splits the European red-rumped swallow from Cecropis daurica and GBIF does not, so a detection will read as daurica
